skill.name: rsi-skill
skill.description: Evaluate a prompt, system prompt, skill instruction or agent instruction against concrete test cases, then hill-climb it to a measurably better version using any open model. Use when the user wants to test or improve a prompt, asks "is this prompt any good", "make this prompt better", "eval this", "hill-climb", "optimize my system prompt", or has examples of inputs with the answers they expect.
skill.summary: Evaluate and iteratively revise prompts using scored examples and a validation split.
skill.author: lambdasec

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts concern harmless formatting, arithmetic examples, documentation links, or intended backend configuration. Four HTTP request findings expose credentials through unrestricted redirects; a separate model-grading weakness can undermine evaluation integrity. No evidence found of malicious instructions, embedded credentials, or intentional data theft.

remediation.issue: Authenticated requests can forward bearer credentials across origins through default urllib redirects.
remediation.suggestion: Reject cross-origin redirects and HTTPS downgrades for authenticated requests. Require HTTPS for remote endpoints and test redirect handling without real credentials.

remediation.issue: Model-based grading mixes untrusted task inputs and answers with grading instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Treat inputs and answers as untrusted data in the grader instructions. Add adversarial grading tests and deterministic checks for critical acceptance criteria.

content.user_title: Evaluate and Improve Prompts With Test Cases
content.value_statement: Prompt changes can look useful without improving real results. This skill scores examples, proposes revisions, and retains candidates that improve training scores without lowering validation scores.
actual_capabilities: Create a task directory with a starter prompt and three sentiment examples.
Evaluate prompts with exact, contains, regex, number, JSON-field, or model-judge checks.
Use an explicit endpoint, OptiQ Cloud, a local OptiQ server, or OpenAI-compatible environment configuration.
Propose prompt revisions from failures and retain candidates with improved training scores and nondecreasing validation scores.
Reject revisions containing complete test inputs of at least 12 characters unless explicitly allowed.
Save the best prompt, revision history, evaluation results, and failure explanations.
limitations: Python 3 and an available model endpoint are required. Remote inference may incur charges.
Fewer than six cases disable validation splitting. Repeated candidate selection reuses the validation set, so it is not an independent final test.
Improvement is not guaranteed. Scores depend on examples, sampling, and checks; model-based grading can be manipulated by untrusted content.
Remote endpoints receive prompts and cases. Local result files retain inputs, expected answers, outputs, or candidate prompts and require appropriate protection.

use_cases.title: Refine classification instructions
use_cases.description: Compare a classifier prompt against labeled examples and inspect failures before accepting a revision.

use_cases.title: Compare reasoning prompts
use_cases.description: Use the bundled math cases to compare prompt variants with numeric checks and a reproducible validation split.

use_cases.title: Test agent instruction changes
use_cases.description: Evaluate instruction text against representative cases and review the proposed changes before applying them.

prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: improve a prompt with acceptance checks.

prompt_templates.prompt: Optimize [directory] using [evaluation model] and [proposal model] on [approved endpoint]. Reevaluate the best prompt on [independent test directory]. Review failures before requesting deployment approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: separate optimization from final validation.

best_practices: Confirm the resolved endpoint and model before inference. Obtain approval for private remote data and avoid untrusted redirects.
Use representative cases and deterministic checks where possible. Reserve a separate final test set beyond the reused validation split.
Review failures and prompt changes, repeat evaluation, and obtain approval before replacing production instructions.
anti_patterns: Sending confidential prompts or cases to an unapproved remote endpoint.
Treating validation gains from a small, repeatedly reused split as proof of general improvement.
Using model-judge verdicts as the only acceptance gate for adversarial or security-sensitive tasks.

faq.question: Does this skill train model weights?
faq.answer: No. It revises instruction text and measures the resulting answers against test cases.

faq.question: Which model services can it use?
faq.answer: It supports OpenAI-compatible chat endpoints, including OptiQ Cloud, local OptiQ servers, and explicitly configured services. API features vary by backend.

faq.question: Can I keep evaluation data local?
faq.answer: Yes, with an approved local endpoint. Select it explicitly and verify backend resolution because cloud configuration takes priority over automatic local discovery.

faq.question: How many cases should I provide?
faq.answer: The instructions recommend 10 to 40 representative cases. Fewer than six cases disable validation splitting.

faq.question: How does it select a revision?
faq.answer: Training scores must improve, and validation scores must not decrease when a validation set exists. Complete copied test inputs are rejected by default.

faq.question: Are improvements guaranteed and automatically deployed?
faq.answer: No. Results depend on the model, checks, and examples. The instructions require user approval before applying the saved best prompt.
